e.etymology: The Italian and Spanish form of Greek Arsenios, from arsen, masculine or virile. Saint Arsenius the Great was a Roman tutor who became a desert hermit in Egypt.
namesakes: Arsenio Hall (comedian and late-night talk-show host)

e.etymology: A spelling of Mariah, an English form of Maria that keeps the old pronunciation with a long i. Maria goes back to Hebrew Miryam, a name of uncertain meaning.

The English title, from Old English hlaefdige, the mistress of a household, literally bread kneader. It was a given name in the US around 1900 and is used today in Colombia, where it is also spelled Leidy.

assoc.t: cocker spaniel in Disney's Lady and the Tramp

e.note: Reads as a title or form of address rather than a name, and it is a common name for dogs.

e.etymology: A 1990s American name, a feminine form of Keon or a spelling in the family of Kiana and Kiona.
French form of Clarissa, a medieval Latin name for a nun of the Order of Saint Clare, built on Clara, from Latin clarus, bright or clear. Clarice is its English counterpart.
namesakes: Clarisse McClellan (the curious teenager in Fahrenheit 451)
Clarisse La Rue (daughter of Ares in the Percy Jackson books)

e.etymology: A respelling of Jalen, an American name popularized in the 1990s by basketball player Jalen Rose, whose mother formed it from the names James and Leonard.
The Spanish feminine of Agustín, from Latin Augustinus, a derivative of augustus, venerable or majestic, the title of the first Roman emperor.
A modern American name that follows the pattern of Amya, Jamya and Samya.
The form of Theodora used across southern and eastern Europe, from Greek theos, God, and doron, gift. The sixth-century Byzantine empress Theodora is its most famous bearer.
A respelling of Mason, the English occupational surname for a stoneworker, from Old French maçon, written to echo Macy. It is given mostly to girls.
A modern American name that joins Jay to the -onna ending of Deonna and Keonna.
A spelling of Electra that keeps the Greek k, from elektron, amber. In Greek myth Electra is the daughter of Agamemnon who helps avenge his murder.
namesakes: Elektra Natchios (Marvel assassin played on film by Jennifer Garner)

assoc.t: Marvel Comics assassin tied to Daredevil

e.etymology: The Persian and Urdu form of Daniel, borrowed through Arabic Daniyal from Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge. Daniel is honored as a prophet in Islam as well as in Judaism and Christianity.
The Italian word gioia, joy, used as a girls' name, the equivalent of English Joy.
A modern American name that joins the sound of Cameron to the -arion ending of Jamarion and Damarion.
A modern American name related to Bria and Breanna, with a spelling that echoes Freya.
English form of the Irish name Íde, traditionally linked to Old Irish ítu, thirst. Saint Ita of Killeedy was a sixth-century Irish abbess. Ita is also a Yiddish and German short form related to Ida.
A respelling of Tate, an English surname from the Old English personal name Tata, whose meaning is uncertain.
A respelling of Zaire, the former name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of the Congo River, a Portuguese rendering of a Kikongo word for river.
A respelling of Amani, which means peace in Swahili and wishes or hopes in Arabic.
A spelling of Romy, a German pet form of Rosemarie made famous by actress Romy Schneider. Romey is also a surname of German origin.
An English surname taken from the village of Caston in Norfolk, now used as a given name in the style of Paxton and Easton.
A modern American blend of Miya or Mia with Anna.
A respelling of Zayden, an American coinage that puts a Z on the -ayden sound of Aiden, Jayden and Kayden.
In Japanese, Riku is often written with the character for land, though other characters are used. In Finnish it is a pet form of Rikhard, the local form of Richard.
namesakes: Riku (Sora's friend and rival in the Kingdom Hearts video games)

assoc.t: Riku, Sora's rival in the Kingdom Hearts games

e.etymology: A phonetic spelling of Nico or Niko, short forms of Nicholas, from Greek nike, victory, and laos, people.

assoc.t: Neeko, a champion in the game League of Legends

e.etymology: A respelling of Leilani, from Hawaiian lei, a garland of flowers, and lani, heaven or sky. In Hawaiian poetry lei can also stand for a beloved child.
Turkish Aslı, genuine or original, from Arabic asl, origin or root. Somali families use it too. In Turkish folk literature Aslı is the beloved in the romance of Kerem and Aslı.
From Hebrew Yehoash, usually read as Yahweh has given. Several Old Testament figures bear it, including a king of Judah crowned as a child and the father of Gideon.
A modern American name built on Sky or Skyler with the -len ending of Jaylen and Kaylen.
A surname, borne by the Spanish saint Paschal Baylon, that fits the sound of modern American names like Braylon and Jaylon.
A respelling of Lincoln, the English city whose name joins Celtic lindo, pool, and Latin colonia, settlement. The surname became a first name in honor of Abraham Lincoln.
